method: park RX1 gain either side of the low-power threshold and sample CTRL_OUT7 200 times in a tight builtin loop
next: needs the FPGA stage, or a finer level control than 1 dB gain steps
prediction: the low-power bit changes state no faster than one power-measurement period; predicted 256-410 us

provenance.harness: TX2 -> 30 dB pad -> bare SMA tee -> RX1/RX2 (tee has ~0 dB port-to-port isolation; see docs/learnings.md harness entry)
provenance.source: own TX2 fpga_dds tone at +100 kHz, TX2 hardwaregain 0 dB (full scale)

reading: The bit is a stable level on both sides of a sharp threshold at 22 dB: 200/200 high at 20-21 dB, 0/200 high at 22-24 dB, and zero transitions anywhere. With no dither there is no interval to measure. Two limits compound: the sampler runs at about 237 us against a predicted 256-410 us period, and RX gain is quantised to 1 dB, which is likely too coarse to park the comparator exactly at its trip point where it would dither.
